blocks.DESERT00: Flat open sand with a few walkable rocks, skulls, bones and a snake; no real cover.
blocks.DESERT01: Flat open sand with a few small rocks, a pit, tumbleweed and a scorched patch; no cover.
blocks.DESERT02: Flat open sand dotted with green scrub and two broken cacti; no cover.
blocks.DESERT03: Two low sand mounds (8 high): a 3x3 one in the NW and a 5x5 one in the centre-east, plus a saguaro, barrel cactus and rocks on the west side.
blocks.DESERT04: Two small low dunes (NE 4x4, SW 3x3), a saguaro/flowering cactus pair in the north-west and a lone barrel cactus; otherwise open.
blocks.DESERT05: Open sand with scattered impassable cacti (saguaro, barrel, flowering) and two dead trees; light cover.
blocks.DESERT06: Dense cactus grove in the centre-north and south-west plus rocks to the east: the most cover in the desert set.
blocks.DESERT07: One 8x8 dune filling the block, rising in two tiers to a flat 16-high top; ramps on every side.
blocks.DESERT08: A 10x10 dune rising in three tiers to a 4x4 full-height (one storey) summit in the centre with a rock on top.
blocks.DESERT09: 20x20: two long dune ridges running roughly north-south (west one tops out at 16, east one reaches full-height summits) with a narrow sand valley between them; open sand on the edges.
blocks.DESERT10: 20x20 mesa: almost the whole block is a three-tier dune whose huge flat full-height (one storey) top carries cacti, rocks and a dead tree; ramps all round, flat sand only at the very edges.
blocks.DESERT11: 20x20 mostly open sand with four low mounds (one with a 16-high step), a cactus grove in the centre-west and rocks, dead trees and cacti in the north-west corner.
blocks.MOUNT00: Flat open stony ground with grass, mud and puddle patches; no cover.
blocks.MOUNT01: Flat open ground with dark rock cracks and two brown mud patches; no cover.
blocks.MOUNT02: Flat open grassy ground with a crack and two mud patches; no cover.
blocks.MOUNT03: A small 4x5 rock rise (8 high) in the north-centre and a 2x2 knoll to the south-east; boulder cluster, white boulders and a hollow log on the west.
blocks.MOUNT04: Flat ground with plenty of single-tile cover: boulder cluster in the NW, white boulders, a tree stump and hollow logs.
blocks.MOUNT05: A big low hill nearly filling the block, two tiers up to a 16-high plateau; ramps on all sides.
blocks.MOUNT06: A three-tier hill rising to a 2x2 full-height rock summit in the centre with grass on top.
blocks.MOUNT07: A one-storey rock plateau over most of the block (cliff faces to the south and east, ramps on the north and east edges); boulders, a dead tree and grass on top.
blocks.MOUNT08: A one-storey cliff plateau in the west/north-west with sheer faces; terraced slopes descend to the south-east; logs, grass and mud on top.
blocks.MOUNT09: A one-storey rock plateau in the east-centre with cliff faces south and east and ramps from the north-west; dead trees and boulders on top.
blocks.MOUNT10: A rock pinnacle in the centre: a ramp ring around a one-storey core, then two more sheer storeys of cliff (upper terraces reachable only by flying); open ground around it.
blocks.MOUNT11: 20x20 big hill: three-tier ramps on all sides up to a broad one-storey plateau, on which a second smaller hill climbs to two-storey rock outcrops with boulders; dead trees and a crevice in the NW corner.
blocks.MOUNT12: 20x20 massif: a one-storey rock base with cliff faces and inner gullies, topped by a second three-tier hill rising to a large two-storey summit plateau with boulders; ramps up the outer edges, logs and stumps at the corners.
blocks.POLAR00: Flat open snow with an ice hole in the west, a crevasse in the north-east, a pressure ridge in the south and some dirt patches; no cover.
blocks.POLAR01: Flat open snow with brown dirt patches, a snow drift and ice rubble; no cover.
blocks.POLAR02: Flat open snow with two crevasses and a cracked-ice ring; no cover.
blocks.POLAR03: Snow with two 2x2 ice outcrops, a fallen ice slab, two small snow mounds in the west and an ice hole in the north-east.
blocks.POLAR04: A 4x5 snow mound (8 high) in the north-centre, two small 2x2 mounds and an ice outcrop in the south-west.
blocks.POLAR05: Several small 2x2 snow mounds and a 4x4 mound in the south-east, an ice hole, a snow drift and a cracked-ice ring.
blocks.POLAR06: Four 4x4 snow mounds (8 high) in the corners with a crevasse and a pressure ridge between them; open snow crossroads through the middle.
blocks.POLAR07: Four small frozen ponds (impassable water) near the corners, open snow between them.
blocks.POLAR08: A roughly 6x6 lake (impassable) in the centre with open snow around it.
blocks.POLAR09: Two L-shaped water channels along the west and east edges with a snow corridor running north-south through the middle.
blocks.POLAR10: Two long lakes along the north and south edges with an east-west strip of snow through the middle.
blocks.POLAR11: One big lake filling nearly the whole block; only a thin snow rim around the edge.
blocks.POLAR12: 20x20 mostly water: large lakes with a winding snow causeway running from the south-west to the north-east and two small snow islands.
blocks.POLAR13: 20x20 mostly water with winding snow paths along the edges and through the middle, and several small snow islands.
blocks.MARS00: Flat open Martian sand with a few craterlets; no cover.
blocks.MARS01: Open sand with two small craters and two boulders.
blocks.MARS02: One big crater in the centre, a small crater in the north-west, scattered craterlets.
blocks.MARS03: Crater field: two big craters, two small craters and a couple of boulders.
blocks.MARS04: Two big craters on the east side, two small craters and a rock field in the south-west.
blocks.MARS05: A field of rock piles and boulders across the centre-south (best cover on Mars); one small crater in the north-west.
blocks.MARS06: Dense crater field: four big craters and three small ones.

blocks.MARS08: Solid stepped pyramid pierced by narrow cross-shaped corridors at ground level, with entrances on all four sides.
blocks.MARS09: Stepped pyramid with a ground-level alien chamber and a second-storey chamber above it (with a lift tile); entrances on the west and east sides.
blocks.MARS10: Stepped pyramid whose whole ground level is one hollow chamber with a glowing green alien floor; entrance on the east side.

notes:
DIRECTIONS: x+ = east, y+ = south (row 0 of a block is its north edge). Slope names say which way you climb (ramp-*-east climbs toward +x) and corner names say which way the corner rises (corner-out-*-ne rises toward the NE, so it sits at the hill's SW corner).
HILLS (DESERT and MOUNT share the exact same layout of records 27-65): three tiers of 12 objects each: low = 27-38 (ground to 8, terrainLevel -4), mid = 41-52 (8 to 16, -12), high = 54-65 (16 to 24, -20); flat fills: 39 = raised-8, 53 = raised-16, 40 = full-height block (24). Inside each tier the order is: outer-NE, ramp-E, outer-SE, ramp-S, outer-SW, ramp-N, ramp-W, outer-NW, inner-NE, inner-SW, inner-NW, inner-SE (verified from neighbour heights across every map block). A hill is built on ONE level as concentric rings: outermost ring = low tier (ramps on the edges facing outward: north edge uses ramp-low-south, west edge ramp-low-east, etc.; outer corners at the 4 convex corners, inner corners at concave turns), next ring inward = mid tier, next = high tier, centre = sand-block/rock-block. Tiers can be skipped by using raised-8 or raised-16 as the flat top (DESERT03 is a 3x3 mound: 29 30 31 / 28 39 33 / 27 32 34). The top of a full block (40) is walkable at the next level's height; DESERT leaves the level above empty, MOUNT puts ordinary floors (mountain-ground/grass/mud) on z+1 above its blocks and may start another set of slope rings on z+1 on top of the blocks (MOUNT11/12: a second hill on the plateau). Sheer cliffs = full blocks next to lower ground with no ramp; MOUNT uses rock-cliff-1/2/3 (66-68) instead of 40 on the exposed edge tiles purely for the look, and stacks blocks on z1/z2 for multi-storey cliffs (MOUNT10). In MOUNT, 40, 53 and 66-68 are bigWall (fill the whole tile).
POLAR has only the low tier (19-31, ground to 8) in a different order: 19 outer-NE, 20 ramp-E, 21 outer-SE, 22 ramp-S, 23 outer-SW, 24 outer-NW, 25 ramp-N, 26 ramp-W, 27 flat raised-8, 28 inner-NE, 29 inner-SW, 30 inner-NW, 31 inner-SE (30 used once; its direction is inferred by elimination). A 2x2 snow mound = 21 23 / 19 24.
POLAR lakes: all water tiles (0, 63-80) are impassable floors (tuWalk 255). Build a lake as: corners 69 NW / 71 NE / 70 SW / 72 SE, edges 64|67 north, 76 south, 63|66 west, 77 east, open water inside (78/79/80/68, floes 73-75); concave turns use 65 (land NW, a floor) and objects 61 (land NE), 60 (land SE), 62 (land SW).
MARS pyramids: each storey is a ring of side/corner pieces (impassable sloped faces) around pyramid-block fill, each storey one tile smaller on every side than the one below; MARS07-10 are 8x8 at z0 down to 2x2 (corners only) at z3. Hollow interiors and the doors/walls/floors inside them come from U_WALL02 (not labelled here). Mars crater rims (10-21) are walkable objects raised 4-8.
The 'die' numbers in the sheets behave like LOCAL indices into the same dataset (e.g. DESERT cactus 10 -> 11 broken cactus, sand floors -> 21 scorched sand, MOUNT 71 -> 73 -> 75), not global ids.
Oddities: DESERT09 has a stray rock (26) and sand floor floating on z2 at x14-15,y1; MOUNT floors list die 76 (log debris) which looks like an original data quirk; MARS 34/35 (metal frame) and 29 (pyramid apex) and MOUNT 74/76 are never used in the original maps. MOUNT crack floors 8-14 are combined freely (e.g. 11 9 / 8 10 in MOUNT07, 11 13 / 12 14 in MOUNT11), so only one 2x2 combo is given as a multi. Desert rocks and Mars rock piles/crater rims are walkable; cacti, dead trees, boulders and logs are not.
